The four readers

A listing is read by people who never talk to each other.

Most listings are written for none of them. Each reader has three questions that stop or stall a deal.

READER 01

Security reviewer

Where is customer data stored? Which reports can you share? How is data deleted?

READER 02

Procurement

What exactly is one pricing unit? What happens if we go over? What support comes with the price?

READER 03

Technical evaluator

How is it deployed? Which AWS services does it connect to? How long to the first working result?

READER 04

AI search

What does it do, for whom, and what evidence backs the claims? Written so a model can summarise it.

Questions

Straight answers.

What changes after the optimize?

Security reviewers find their answers on the listing instead of emailing you. Procurement can see what one unit buys. AI search can tell who the product is for and what it does. Re-run the audit and you see the new score.

What do you need from us?

Your listing URL, product website, pricing, and a one-pager or deck if you have one. Anything you can prove, such as certifications, integrations or customers, goes into the listing. Anything you cannot prove stays out.

Do you need access to our AWS account?

Not for the optimize: you paste the new copy yourself. For a launch you choose: grant temporary IAM access that you revoke once the listing is live, or we hand your team every field ready to enter.

What do we have to build for a launch?

AWS requires SaaS products to connect for sign-up and billing, and that is code in your product, built by your engineers. We handle the listing, the pricing setup and the AWS approval. The 14 days run from the point that integration is ready, and we scope that with you first.

Our product is not an AI agent. Does this apply?

Yes. Six of the seven dimensions apply to any product on AWS Marketplace. Protocol & category fit only counts if you tick “AI agents call this product”. Otherwise it is left out and your score is out of the 60 points that apply.

Is this an official AWS score?

No. It is an independent audit of the listing text, using the same fixed checks on every listing. It shows what a buyer, reviewer or AI search can find on the page. It does not predict AWS approval, search placement or sales.

How is the benchmark built?

Live AWS Marketplace listings read through the AWS Marketplace Discovery API, at most two per seller so large sellers do not skew it, each scored with the same audit. Only aggregate numbers are published, never a single listing’s score.

Why not let AI rewrite the listing?

AI drafts words. It does not know which reviewer questions your listing leaves open, or which claims you can prove. Every line we write uses your facts only.
